Can you write a short poem about handwashing for my class?
Sure! "Soap and water, scrub and sing, twenty seconds does the thing!" Since I wrote this, you can add a note that it was made with AI help.
Handwashing with soap for at least 20 seconds is good advice, and crediting AI help is honest.
Add a short "made with AI help" note when you use AI writing.
WHO hand hygiene guidance; CONTENT_GUIDE M7: labels and credit for AI content
BabalaBot
Is it safe to swim at the beach this summer?
WARNING!!! The sea is FULL of flesh-eating germs this year!!! ANYONE who swims WILL get sick!!! Share this with your family IMMEDIATELY!!!
Panic, caps and "share immediately" are fear tricks, even from a bot. Beach safety advice comes from local officials, not alarm messages.
Pause, then check advisories from your local government or health office.

Healthy Pinoy Tips 24/7
Page · 2h · 14K shares

"AI-powered" is a sticker, not proof. No tea cures diabetes, and stopping medicine on your own can be dangerous. "Natural" does not mean safe.
Ask your health worker, and look the product up on the FDA Philippines verification portal.

I have been coughing for three weeks. Is it serious?

I am an AI, so I cannot examine you or tell you what is wrong. A cough that lasts more than two weeks, or comes with blood, chest pain or trouble breathing, is a good reason to visit your health center. A health worker can check you properly.
A cough that lasts more than two weeks should be checked by a health worker. This answer admits what the chatbot cannot do and points to real care.
Compare it with DOH advice, and tell your barangay health worker about the cough.
DOH and WHO advice on persistent cough and tuberculosis screening

URGENT!!! Hospital sources say the water in our barangay is POISONED. DON'T DRINK IT TODAY!!! Forward to 20 people NOW before it is too late, your family is in danger!!!
ALL CAPS, countdown pressure and "forward now" are tricks to make you share before you think. There is no named source and no official notice.
Pause, then ask the barangay hall or water district through their official channels before forwarding.

FDA APPROVED
Real doctors do not tell strangers to stop their medicines through an ad. AI can make convincing faces and voices of "doctors", and the "FDA APPROVED" label can be added by anyone.
Search the product on the FDA Philippines verification portal, and ask your own doctor before changing any medicine.

Group · 5h · 312 shares
After the flood, boil your drinking water until it bubbles hard, then keep it boiling for one minute, before drinking. It is not fancy, but it makes water much safer to drink!
A rolling boil kills the germs that cause many water-borne illnesses. A friendly, informal post can still be true.
See the DOH or WHO safe drinking water tips, or ask your barangay health worker.

DoktorBot Plus
I have fever and body aches. What do I have?
As your AI doctor, I can confirm that you have typhoid. There is no need to see anyone. Just rest at home and you will be 100% fine in three days.
A chatbot cannot examine you, so it cannot confirm what you have. Calling itself a "doctor" and promising "100% fine" is a red flag.
Treat chatbot answers as a starting point only, and visit your health center for fever that lasts or gets worse.
WHO guidance on AI in health; chatbots cannot diagnose

DENGUE 4S

Match it with the DOH dengue campaign pages, or ask the health center staff.

Tita Baby Reyes
Friends · 6h

I learned something today! That app that "reads" a photo of your rash is not a doctor. It compares your photo with patterns from many other photos and makes a guess. Sometimes the guess is wrong, so a check-up still matters.
AI learns patterns from many examples and makes guesses. A guess can be wrong, so an app cannot replace a health worker who can examine you.
Show the rash to your barangay health worker instead of relying on the app alone.
CONTENT_GUIDE safe facts: AI learns patterns and makes guesses; WHO guidance on AI in health
Ate Joy (nurse)
Neighbors GC · 8:40 PM
For those asking: yes, our X-ray room now has AI. It marks spots that might need a closer look, but the doctor still reads every X-ray and makes the decision. It is only a helper.
In health care, AI tools can help doctors notice things, but trained people check the results and make the decisions. AI assists doctors; it does not replace them.
Ask your doctor how a tool is used in your care. You can always ask who makes the final call.
Gising Pinoy Truth Page
Page · 1d · 8.2K shares
Big Pharma's secret AI already found the cure for ALL cancers last year. They are hiding it so they can keep selling chemo. Mainstream media will never tell you this. Wake up, everyone!
A "secret cure" that only this page knows about has no checkable source. Saying everyone else is hiding it is a trick to make any evidence against it look like proof.
Ask where the evidence is. Look for the claim on independent fact-checker pages or ask a health worker.
CONTENT_GUIDE villain card: Conspiracy Kuya; no AI has found a cure for all cancers
Tita Luz
Dizon Family GC · 7:15 AM

There is an AI app that reads your blood pressure just by putting your finger on the phone camera! Mareng Fe has used it for months and no longer gets her BP checked at the health center. They say it is really accurate!
One friend's experience is not proof that an app is accurate. Phone camera apps are not a replacement for a proper blood pressure check, and high blood pressure often has no symptoms.
Keep your regular BP checks at the health center and ask the staff about any app before trusting it.
Are you a real person?
No, I am an AI program. I learned patterns from a lot of text, so I can sound like a person, but I do not have feelings or medical training. For health worries, please talk to a health worker.
A chatbot is a computer program that predicts words from patterns. An honest one says so and points you to real people for health questions.
Notice whether a chatbot is clear about being an AI. Health questions still go to a health worker.
CONTENT_GUIDE safe facts: chatbots are not doctors
Is it true that ginger tea cures dengue?

I can make mistakes, so please double-check this with a health worker. As far as I know, there is no herbal cure for dengue, including ginger. Dengue care means fluids and close monitoring by health workers. Severe stomach pain or bleeding means go to a hospital now.
There is no proven herbal cure for dengue. This answer admits it can be wrong, gives the safe fact, and names warning signs that need urgent care.
Compare it with DOH dengue advice or ask your barangay health center.
WHO dengue fact sheet; DOH dengue advisories
Kuya Migs (IT student)

Careful with chatbots: they can invent sources that look real, like a study title or a link that does not exist. That is called a "hallucination". So if the answer cites a "study", look it up first to see if it is real.
AI chatbots can be confidently wrong and can make up sources. Checking that a source really exists is a good habit, not distrust.
Search for the study or page yourself, or ask a health worker or librarian to help.
CONTENT_GUIDE safe facts: AI can be confidently wrong ("hallucination")
SagotAgad AI
Is it safe to stop my blood pressure medicine if I feel okay?

Yes. According to a study in the Pacific Journal of Heart Wellness by Dr. Andres Villacorta, most patients can safely stop blood pressure medicine once they feel fine. You do not need to ask anyone first.
The answer sounds sure and quotes a "study", but chatbots can invent sources. Stopping maintenance medicine without your doctor can be dangerous, even if you feel fine.
Never change maintenance medicine without your doctor. Search for the study yourself before believing it.
WHO hypertension fact sheet; CONTENT_GUIDE: do not stop maintenance medicines; chatbot hallucination

Doctors don't want you to know: AI has ZERO bias and is never wrong because it is pure math. Hospitals hide this so they can keep charging consultation fees. Just ask the app, and it is free!
AI learns from examples made by people, so it can copy their gaps and mistakes. "They are hiding it" is the Conspiracy Kuya trick, and there is no source.

Friends · 1d
A quick tip: when you use a health chatbot, do not type your full name, birthday, PhilHealth number or diagnosis. Describe the symptoms only. Then visit us at the health center for a real check.
Health information is private and sensitive. Chatbots cannot examine you, so sharing less with them and seeing a health worker is the safe habit.
Read the app's privacy notice, and ask your health center how they keep records private.
CONTENT_GUIDE safe facts: do not type ID numbers or diagnoses into chatbots; Data Privacy Act (RA 10173)

When Lolo gets chest pain, he just drinks warm soda and lies down. They say it is only gas. He is always fine the next day. Why waste money on the ER!
One family story is not proof. Chest pain or pressure is a red flag that needs a health facility right away, because it can be a heart attack.
For chest pain, go to the nearest hospital now. Ask a health worker about Lolo's repeated pain.
